method:
Twenty-five further hypotheses in five batches, following up the strongest leads of batches.py.

Same conventions: a null for each test, one-sided p-values, and Benjamini-Hochberg at a 5% false-discovery rate
across the twenty-five. Helpers and data come from batches.py.

results.hypothesis: At Knossos, words with undeciphered signs are more often personal names
Knossos-only words are more Linear A-like than words shared by Knossos and Pylos
At Knossos, names follow Linear A syllable rates more closely than common words
Cretan place names in Linear B are more Linear A-like than mainland place names
Knossos adjectives in -jo/-ja are built on Linear A words (stem + suffix)
Largest-first listing holds outside Haghia Triada too
The even-amount preference is stronger for grain than for men
Amounts on the same tablet are doubles of each other more than chance
KI-RO entries are mostly single units (1)
Liquids (wine, oil) take fractions more often than dry goods
Words ending -TI are entry labels (names) rather than headings
Words beginning A- are headings rather than entry labels
Words ending -JA belong to the religious register
The first and last syllables of a word share their vowel more than chance
Long words are compounds of attested shorter words more than chance
Roundels and nodules carry different signs
Sealing signs are the first signs of the commonest administrative words
Religious inscriptions use word dividers more than tablets
After a KU-RO total, the next line opens with a new commodity
Peak-sanctuary inscriptions share vocabulary with each other more than with other religious objects
